title: Malaria in Tanzania: Practical Prevention
excerpt: Malaria is present in much of Tanzania. Practical ways to prevent mosquito bites and what to discuss with your doctor.
body:
Malaria is transmitted by mosquitoes and occurs in many parts of Tanzania, including safari areas and Zanzibar. Higher areas such as the upper slopes of Kilimanjaro have lower risk.

## Prevent bites

- Use insect repellent with DEET or another effective active ingredient.
- Wear long sleeves and trousers at dusk and in the evening.
- Sleep under a mosquito net or in a room with screens.
- Many lodges spray rooms in the evening.

## Medication

Antimalarial medication can be part of prevention. Which medication is suitable depends on you; discuss this with your doctor or travel clinic.

## Symptoms

Fever, chills, headache and muscle pain, even weeks after your return. If you get a fever, see a doctor quickly and mention your trip.

## Children

Malaria prevention for children needs specific advice.

This is general information, not medical advice. See [vaccinations](/blog/tanzania-vaccinations/) and [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
